review.recommendation: Approve as-is; ship the working-tree diff unchanged. Basis (observed from the packet, not inferred): (1) The round-13 gap is closed by the correct instrument — an unfiltered `grep -rn "kstack-jira" . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=node_modules` with no `--include`, whose 89 hits are fully accounted for (56 QC archives + 18 review archives + 2 decisions + 1 reflexion-lessons + 11 live + 1 test file = 89), plus a second search keyed on exit-status *idioms* (`$?`, `PIPESTATUS`, `.status`, `.exitCode`, `child_process`/`spawn`/`exec`/`Popen`, `process.exitCode`) rather than the CLI name. The idiom search is the load-bearing one, since a consumer could shell out via a variable rather than a literal string; it returned only kstack-jira.mjs-internal matches. Each of the 11 live references is individually triaged and none branches on status. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:29` runs `npm test` only. (2) Code correctness re-verified against the diff: `youngestMarkerAgeMs` now returns `null` for every unmeasurable case (non-finite clock, unparseable marker, non-finite or negative age) and `Infinity` for no markers; both of the exactly three grep-confirmed occurrences (def at 1069, call at 1120 in runVerification, call at 1169 in preMutationDuplicateGate) test `null` explicitly before any comparison and never do arithmetic on it, so the sentinel-coercion hazard has no live instance. `gateExitCode()` preserves DUPLICATE precedence via `gate.keys?.length` and emits 20 only for the single `reason: INDEX_LAG` branch, which is reachable only after `result.kind === 'matches'` with zero keys and a measurable sub-floor age — matching the documented meaning exactly. Poll exhaustion, search failure, unmeasurable age, and submit's retry-verification wait all still return 2, and there is a dedicated test asserting the first two stay at 2. (3) Documentation is consistent across all three surfaces that carry an exit inventory (`--help` template literal, `JIRA_QUEUE.md`, spec deviation note), and the `grep -rln "exit code\|exit-code\|EXIT\."` over `skills/*/SKILL.md` returning zero matches establishes that no SKILL.md can hold a stale list. (4) The EXIT-inventory test now pins `[0,1,2,3,6,8,9,13,14,15,16,17,18,19,20]`, asserts `STATE_ERROR===2` and `INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED===20` individually, and still asserts the 10–12 retirement — so a future renumbering that reintroduces a collision fails loudly. (5) The diff-content SHA-256 over the four files, in the same order as embedded, is the right artifact to bind "these tests passed" to "this exact text," which is stronger than round 12's HEAD-only binding. No follow-up work is required before merge. Optional, non-blocking hygiene for a later pass: `VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG` ('index-lag') is the control-flow reason while the audit record for the same condition writes 'marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum'; two names for one state is a readability nit, not a defect, and the tests pin the audit string that operators actually see.
review.strongestObjection: The consumer audit is necessarily bounded by the repository: it proves no in-repo caller branches on exit 2 from kstack-jira, but this is a *plugin*, and an installation elsewhere (an operator's wrapper script, a hook, another repo's CI) could hold a `case 2:` / exit-code allowlist that now receives 20 for a case that previously returned 2 — including on a `submit --dry-run` path, as the changed test at tests/jira-queue.test.mjs:377 demonstrates. No repository-internal grep of any file-type breadth can observe that, so the evidence supplied this round, while methodologically correct, cannot retire the risk in principle. It is mitigated rather than eliminated: 20 is nonzero, so any generic `code !== 0` handling is unaffected, and the failure direction is fail-safe (a consumer that does not recognize 20 treats the operation as failed, which it was — the mutation was refused). The realistic worst case is a consumer that logs "unexpected exit code" instead of "waiting on index lag," i.e. degraded operator messaging, never a false-clear or a duplicate ticket. This is the same residual disclosed in round 11 and is correctly characterized in the packet; it is a reason not to claim 100, not a reason to withhold approval.
unresolvedQuestions: Out-of-repo exit-code contract surface: is there any published or distributed artifact for this plugin (marketplace/plugin manifest description, top-level README, install docs, or an operator runbook kept outside this repo) that enumerates kstack-jira exit codes and would now be stale by omitting 20? The in-repo greps establish that plugins/kstack/references/JIRA_QUEUE.md is the only in-tree inventory, but a distribution-side description is outside what those greps can observe. Non-blocking — a stale external list omitting 20 is a documentation gap, not a behavioral break, since 20 remains nonzero and the refusal semantics are unchanged.
